capabilities: Sync vault files through S3-compatible buckets or WebDAV
Merge concurrent edits line by line and keep both copies when it cannot
Restore files, folders or the whole vault to earlier versions
Share folders with roles, expiring invites and signed changes
Publish selected notes as a static website in separate storage
disambiguation: Not a password manager or encrypted-notes vault; it syncs, shares and publishes existing vault files through storage you provide.
extras: Free, open source (MIT), no account and no telemetry. Tested on macOS and iOS only; Android not yet supported and no independent security audit. The first branch upgrade makes the vault unreadable to versions before 0.12.0, and the README advises keeping a backup of important vaults.
intentEvidence: Coffer is for people who want their vault in storage that they control.
problem: Syncing a vault through storage you control otherwise means paying for Obsidian Sync or running a server for a self-hosted sync tool.

relations.evidence: Obsidian Sync is the official sync service. It needs no setup, and your subscription supports the Obsidian team.
Remotely Save supports more storage services, such as Dropbox and OneDrive.
Self-hosted LiveSync syncs in real time (with CouchDB, or peer-to-peer while both devices are online).
Obsidian Git gives full Git history and diffs with any Git host.
iCloud Drive is built into Apple devices and needs no plugin.

summary: End-to-end encrypted vault sync through your own S3-compatible bucket or WebDAV server, with version history, shared folders and static site publishing.
